full.description: This is a gross pathology photograph showing a cardiac valve, specifically the aortic valve viewed from the aortic aspect. The valve leaflets exhibit nodular thickening, calcification, and restricted mobility along the closure lines. These features are characteristic of calcific aortic stenosis or degenerative aortic valve disease. The surrounding aortic root tissue is also visible.

The image also demonstrates marked left atrial dilation as viewed from above the valve. These findings are consistent with aortic coarctation and associated cardiovascular remodeling.

random.description: This image shows a gross specimen of an aortic or pulmonary heart valve viewed from above. The valve cusps are visibly thickened, fibrotic, and contain prominent nodular calcifications along their closing margins. These degenerative changes are characteristic of calcific aortic stenosis or calcific valvular degeneration. The surrounding myocardium and root structures are also visible.
